Evan: hey everyone 👋 first day here — M2 MacBook Air. switched to fish. trying to bootstrap: asdf for python/node/rust, ran dotfiles/bootstrap. python build fails with openssl configure errors when asdf compiles 3.11. ssh keys don’t persist across reboots (agent not loaded). 1Password CLI prompts for SSO but I don’t have vault access. who should I ping for Okta/VPN/Git? any fish-specific tricks?

Sofia: welcome Evan! for Apple Silicon we point Python builds at Homebrew OpenSSL. in fish I keep this in ~/.config/fish/conf.d/asdf_env.fish:
```
set -x BREW_OPENSSL (brew --prefix openssl@3)
set -x LDFLAGS "-L$BREW_OPENSSL/lib"
set -x CPPFLAGS "-I$BREW_OPENSSL/include"
set -x PKG_CONFIG_PATH "$BREW_OPENSSL/lib/pkgconfig"
env CONFIGURE_OPTS="--with-openssl=$BREW_OPENSSL" asdf install python 3.11.6
```
That usually prevents the configure error.

Sofia: nodejs also needs the asdf node plugin key imported once: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asdf-vm/asdf-nodejs/master/bin/import-release-team-keyring | bash` then `asdf plugin add nodejs` etc.

Sofia: for ssh-agent + fish on mac, I use the keychain method so keys persist:
```
ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
# and in ~/.config/fish/conf.d/ssh.fish:
if not set -q SSH_AUTH_SOCK
  eval (ssh-agent -c) >/dev/null
  ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 >/dev/null 2>&1; or true
end
```
That keeps the agent across restarts and works with VS Code.

Evan: OK tried the BREW_OPENSSL approach and reinstalled python — success 🎉. imported node keyring too. ssh-add --apple-use-keychain fixed persistence after a reboot. still blocked on 1Password/Okta/Git access.

IT: Evan — open an IT ticket at https://itsupport.redwood.internal/new and include your manager's email and employee ID. If you post the ticket number here we can expedite Okta/SSH/Git team invites. Typical ETA 1 business day.

DevOnboard: created onboarding checklist for Evan: [create-ssh-key, add-to-1password, clone-dotfiles, install-asdf-runtimes, request-vpn, grant-git-access] (0/6).

Evan: filed ticket #ONB-903. also one quick question: should I default to using the repo devcontainer or run things locally? interested in consistent env for pair programming.

Sofia: prefer devcontainer when available (consistent toolchain + fewer host quirks). if you need native ARM perf for Rust/GPU work, run locally and coordinate with the service owner. For VS Code + Remote-Containers with fish, make sure devcontainer.json sets the shell to /opt/homebrew/bin/fish so terminals pick up asdf correctly.

IT: Okta invite sent, GitHub teams invite in-flight, VPN ticket in progress. you should get SSO/1Password access shortly.

Evan: got Okta + 1Password. thanks everyone — this got me fully green. tagging here if anything else pops up :heart:
